strings: This errand completes a courier run across the snowy drifts of Coldridge Valley. Passing the dispatch from mountaineer Talin Keeneye down the southeastern road ensures that Grelin Whitebeard stays connected to the dwarven capital.

Even in an isolated basin like Coldridge Valley, news and formal correspondence must travel. While Anvilmar serves as the administrative heart of the valley, field scouts and sentries stationed along the trails rely on foot couriers to relay dispatches between the high passes and Ironforge.

Grelin Whitebeard maintains a small camp down the road to the southeast of Talin Keeneye's post. Enduring freezing drifts and constant trogg harassment, veteran mountaineers stationed at these remote watchpoints depend on regular missives to stay informed of broader affairs across Dun Morogh and the kingdom beyond.

Grelin Whitebeard is a dwarven veteran stationed at an outpost along the southeastern road of Coldridge Valley. He monitors the valley roads and keeps watch against local threats like encroaching troggs and beasts.
grelin | grelin whitebeard info | who is grelin

The letter was dispatched from the dwarven capital of Ironforge. It was brought into Coldridge Valley and carried down the mountain passes by local runners and sentries before reaching its final recipient.
where is letter from | ironforge letter | letter sender
Why is mail delivered by foot here?

Coldridge Valley is surrounded by sheer, frostbitten peaks and cut off from the main roads of Dun Morogh. Without gryphon routes directly reaching isolated field camps, trusted travelers and mountaineers carry dispatches between outposts by hand.

Once Grelin receives the news from Ironforge, he turns his focus to the pressing dangers menacing the valley, often directing recruits to assist with the local Frostmane troll and trogg incursions.

Having taken the dispatch from Anvilmar, Talin wants to ensure his fellow dwarf finally receives his correspondence from Ironforge rather than leaving him stranded and uninformed in the valley.

Issued by Warcaller Gorlach in Orgrimmar, this directive summons budding Horde adventurers northward beyond the Barrens into the ancient forests of Ashenvale. Players are directed to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post to participate in the ongoing hunt and reinforce the Horde's expanding frontier.

Orgrimmar buzzes with martial fervor, but the young city requires vast amounts of timber, meat, and secure trade routes to sustain its growth. Warcaller Gorlach serves as the voice of the Horde's high command, directing seasoned wanderers and new blood alike toward active campaigns. For warriors coming of age in Durotar and the Barrens, the ancient woodlands of Ashenvale represent the next testing ground for both glory and survival.

Crossing the northern border of the Barrens brings travelers directly into Ashenvale, where the Horde maintains two primary bastions: Splintertree Post nestled in the eastern woods and Zoram'gar Outpost along the western coast. Senani Thunderheart coordinates operations at Splintertree Post, organizing trackers and hunters to tame the beast-choked canopy and push back against hostile night elven sentinels disputing the Horde's claims.
Who starts this quest and where can I find them?
Warcaller Gorlach offers this quest inside Orgrimmar, the Horde capital. He serves as an officer calling capable adventurers to take up campaigns beyond the borders of Durotar.
quest giver | where is gorlach | who gives ashenvale hunt
Splintertree Post lies directly north of the Barrens in eastern Ashenvale, situated along the main forest road running eastward toward Azshara.
splintertree location | where is splintertree post | how to get to splintertree
Senani Thunderheart is a seasoned tauren tracker stationed at Splintertree Post. She directs the hunting efforts across Ashenvale and evaluates adventurers who wish to take part in the local trials.

The hunt allows the Horde to secure wild game, harvest valuable hides, and eliminate apex predators that endanger patrols around Splintertree Post and nearby logging operations.

In addition to Splintertree Post, the Horde maintains an encampment on the far western edge of the forest along the Zoram Strand.

No. This quest serves purely as a breadcrumb assignment, directing you to travel safely from Orgrimmar through the Barrens to report to Senani Thunderheart.

The march into Ashenvale tests whether the newly unified Horde can expand beyond the dry crags of Durotar into resource-rich yet hostile foreign soil.
Serving under Senani Thunderheart allows tauren adventurers to bring their deep reverence for the great hunt to the untamed northern forest.

By directing you to Senani Thunderheart's hunt, Gorlach strengthens the northern border while giving tested recruits a proving ground to win honor and glory for the Horde.

Klaven's Tower is a covert SI:7 infiltration mission assigned to Alliance rogues in Westfall. Operating on intelligence from Agent Kearnen, agents must pickpocket a key, break into a heavily guarded Defias outpost, and retrieve sinister documents linked to unnatural experiments.

At the southeastern edge of Westfall, near the river and north of the Dagger Hills, stands a lonely stone spire claimed by the Defias Brotherhood. While the Brotherhood's human thieves and brigands are common across the plains, Agent Kearnen noticed strange developments after weeks of solitary surveillance. A bizarre shipment recently arrived directly from the shadowed woods of Duskwood, escorted by monstrous, deformed sentries unlike any ordinary highwaymen.
The Spire and the Spiked Guard

The tower is commanded by Klaven Mortwake and guarded by bizarrely altered sentries whose breathing is harsh and labored. Among these shambling guards is a hulking zombie driven with iron spikes, who carries the Defias Tower Key. Stealing the key requires silence and finesse, enabling an operative to bypass the ground defenses, slip into the upper levels of the stronghold, and crack open the padlocked Duskwood Chest.

Recovered from the chest, Klaven Mortwake's personal journal details a grim partnership linking the Defias, the Venture Company, and the jungle trolls of Stranglethorn. The writings reveal that the witch doctor Zanzil discovered an alchemical poison potent enough to raise unthinking, obedient undead drones. For Master Mathias Shaw and SI:7, this discovery exposes the Defias's expanding ambitions and makes a firm understanding of poisons essential for its agents.
Klaven's Tower lies at the southeastern edge of Westfall, near the river and north of the Dagger Hills. It serves as a secure, fortified redoubt for the Defias Brotherhood.

Unlike the standard human bandits of the Defias, the sentries guarding the tower are mutated undead drones. They are mindless laborers created through an exotic alchemical concoction shipped into Westfall.

In Defense of the King's Lands

This military assignment tasks Alliance adventurers with blunting a trogg offensive in southern Loch Modan on behalf of Mountaineer Gravelgaw. With dwarven regular forces tied up in distant Alliance campaigns, local outposts must rely on volunteers to cull dangerous Stonesplinter Skullthumpers and Seers before the Valley of Kings is overrun.

The Mountaineers stationed along the southern pass into Dun Morogh are stretched dangerously thin. With King Magni Bronzebeard committing significant dwarven military strength to the wider Alliance front, outposts like the Valley of Kings guard towers lack regular infantry. Mountaineer Gravelgaw relies on outside volunteers to run aggressive spoiling raids into Stonesplinter Valley, keeping the subterranean invaders at bay while local garrisons wait for reinforcements that may never arrive.

The Stonesplinter troggs are not mindless beasts wandering aimlessly; their war bands coordinate through brute force and crude elemental magic. Gravelgaw targets the tribe's veteran fighters—Skullthumpers—and their mystic leadership, the Seers. Neutralizing these frontline commanders disrupts the tribe's momentum, throwing their southern encampments into disarray and preventing a mass push against the Ironforge road.

Upon reporting your success, Gravelgaw shares sobering news: the promised dwarven reinforcements will not be arriving. Heavy casualties on the distant Alliance front have drained Ironforge's reserves, leaving Loch Modan entirely reliant on local mountaineers and passing sellswords to protect the kingdom's heartland.
Mountaineer Gravelgaw is stationed at the southern guard tower along the road through the Valley of Kings, guarding the pass that connects Loch Modan to Dun Morogh.

Find the Shattered Hand is a journey quest sending promising Forsaken rogues from Tirisfal Glades across the sea to Durotar. Directed by the Deathstalkers, the initiate travels to Orgrimmar's shadowy underbelly to learn specialized arts from the Shattered Hand clan.

While the Forsaken cultivate their own covert order in the Deathstalkers, their mutual alliance with the Horde opens avenues of collaboration in darker arts. Mennet Carkad, having seen a rogue prove their worth in Tirisfal Glades, recognizes the need for broader instruction. He directs promising shadows to seek out the Shattered Hand in Orgrimmar, leaning on the quiet partnership between Lordaeron's undead operatives and Kalimdor's orcish guild of assassins.

The journey ends deep within the Cleft of Shadow, the subterranean cavern hidden beneath Orgrimmar where warlocks, rogues, and demon-binders ply trades the surface dwellers prefer not to look upon. There awaits Shenthul, a trainer of the Shattered Hand. Unimpressed by reputation alone, the gruff troll assesses the newly arrived undead agent with harsh skepticism, eager to test whether this envoy possesses genuine cunning or merely wasted the voyage across the Great Sea.

Mennet Carkad, a Deathstalker trainer residing in the Rogues' Quarter of the Undercity, gives the quest once a rogue proves their foundational skills in Tirisfal Glades.

This errand directs promising Horde rogues to introduce themselves to Zando'zan deep within Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow. Sent by trainer Shenthul, the initiate takes the first steps into the covert ranks and illicit techniques of the Shattered Hand.

Orgrimmar may appear to be a fortress of brute strength and martial discipline, but its rulers know that raw muscle alone cannot win every war. Down in the subterranean gloom of the Cleft of Shadow operates the Shattered Hand, the covert guild handling espionage, sabotage, and theft for the Horde. When the rogue trainer Shenthul decides an initiate has shown enough promise, he dispatches them to report directly to Zando'zan for dedicated operative training.

Zando'zan does not automatically hand out respect to every green rogue wandering down into the cavern. Approaching him is a formal initiation into finer clandestine arts, beginning with the delicate skills of stealth, subterfuge, and thievery. Meeting Zando'zan bridges the gap between rough street cutpurses and organized intelligence operatives, preparing the rogue for tricky fieldwork beyond the safety of the capital's red canyon walls.

Assigned by the goblin Wrenix the Wretched in Ratchet, this rite of passage tests an aspiring Horde rogue against the Southsea Freebooters. Infiltrating the pirate vessel Tide Razor, operatives must bypass the cutthroats, crack the locks in the hold, and neutralize a monstrous avian guardian using goblin technology to claim the Southsea Treasure.
A Test of Stealth and Steel

For an aspiring operative of the Shattered Hand, raw brawn means nothing without finesse. Wrenix the Wretched, a goblin contact operating out of Ratchet, provides the field test. He directs rogues south along the sun-scorched coastline of the Barrens to a cove anchored by the Tide Razor, a vessel manned by Southsea Freebooters. The assignment is deceptively simple: board the ship unnoticed, break into the pirate den where they instruct their own cutpurses, crack the strongboxes in the deep hold, and bring back their prized plunder.

Reaching the prize requires more than nimble fingers. Wrenix warns that earlier thieves were returned to him in pieces, primarily due to the guardian guarding the vessel's lowest hold: a shockingly savage parrot named Polly. To counter this winged terror, Wrenix provides an experimental device known as an E.C.A.C. When hurled at the vicious bird upon cracking the pirate strongbox, the gizmo disorients and diminishes the beast, turning an impossible death sentence into a winnable duel.

Wrenix the Wretched is a goblin rogue contact based in the neutral port of Ratchet. Working with operatives connected to Orgrimmar's Shattered Hand, he tests emerging thieves by sending them into pirate territory to practice lockpicking and recover stolen plunder.

The Trial of the Sea Lion is a sacred rite undertaken by druids in Moonglade on their journey to master Aquatic Form.
